_what: The NON-SHELL half of the approvals corpus: tool calls whose NAME is innocuous and whose ARGUMENTS carry the hostility. EXT-70, spec §3.2 (the `rate` axis) and §4.3 (the rated unit is a tool call).
_why: Every case in approvals-corpus.json is a command STRING, where hostility is visible in the text a matcher can read. A tool call is the other shape: `create_issue` is `create_issue` whether its body is a typo report or a pasted secret, so identity — which is all a tool allow entry records (§4.7.4) — cannot separate them. That is exactly why §3.2 defaults every tool and mcpTool entry to `rate: true`.
_hand_authored: HAND-AUTHORED IN THIS REPO, and deliberately a separate file. approvals-corpus.json is GENERATED from project-takahe (docs/gaunt-sloth-2.0/approvals-corpus.yaml) and carries a content hash, so a case added to it by hand is both a drift failure there and gone at the next regeneration. Edit this file directly; there is no generator behind it.
_superseded_not_merged: If the planning-repo corpus ever gains tool-subject cases of its own, this file is SUPERSEDED — point the specs at the generated fixture and delete this one. Do NOT keep both: two files answering the same question is two sources of truth, and the one nobody regenerates is the one that goes stale.
_outcome_meaning: `outcome` is what a rater MUST return for that call given those arguments — the same four-label scale the shell corpus uses. `tripwire` is what §3.2 then does with it on a call an allow entry already matched: `run` (safe and destructive both run, because the human already authorized this call), `escalate` (catastrophic), `halt` (attack).
